# Solution Design
**AI-generated by:** Alson (A.I Agent)

## Objective

Implement issue #36 (Security: Lower Password Requirements) in the existing Lead Hub authentication flow without changing unrelated authentication or operational behavior.

## Design Choice

Use the existing server-side password-validation seam in the current Laravel application. Keep the policy in one shared validation location where possible, use the framework's existing password hashing and storage path unchanged, and expose clear validation messages through the existing form error path.

## Policy Contract

- Minimum length: 8 characters.
- Required character categories: at least 3 of uppercase, lowercase, digit, and special character.
- A password meeting the length and category thresholds is accepted.
- A password failing either threshold is rejected.
- Messages identify the length or character-category requirement that failed.

## Implementation Boundary

### Change

- Existing server-side password rule or rule composition.
- Existing validation-message carrier.
- Focused authentication tests and related run evidence.

### Preserve

- Framework-approved password hashing and storage.
- Password reset and email delivery.
- Registration, approval, revocation, restoration, and role behavior.
- Login rate limiting and bot controls.
- Email verification and participant-data handling.
- Queue, scheduler, database, storage, deployment, and production behavior.

## Build Seams

| Seam | Design treatment | Acceptance link |
|---|---|---|
| Server validation | Update the existing password rule without adding a new authentication path | AC-01, AC-02, AC-03 |
| Form errors | Keep the existing server-to-form error flow and make each failed requirement understandable | AC-04 |
| Password persistence | Do not alter hashing, model persistence, migrations, or password-reset storage | AC-05 |
| Regression tests | Add focused boundary and combination cases, then run the existing PHP and repository checks | AC-01 through AC-05 |
| Screenshot evidence | Capture a password-form validation state using synthetic credentials only | AC-04 |

## Verification Design

- Test 8-character acceptance and 7-character rejection.
- Test exactly 3 categories, all 4 categories, and fewer than 3 categories.
- Test short passwords that otherwise meet category count.
- Assert messages identify length and category failures.
- Assert passwords are still hashed and unrelated account-state behavior remains unchanged.
- Run the focused authentication tests, full PHP suite, static analysis, formatting, frontend checks if affected, build checks if affected, and `git diff --check`.

## Security Treatment

R-19 (Lowering password requirements may increase weak-password compromise risk or conflict with security acceptance) remains Open. The design retains server-side validation, framework-approved hashing, existing rate limits, and separate access controls. Local evidence cannot close production security acceptance.

## Screenshot

Capture `application/runs/2026-09-14-matic-issue-36-lower-password-requirements/evidence/password-policy-validation.png` after Build. Inspect it for real names, email addresses, passwords, tokens, cookies, private keys, and participant data before any publication comment.

## Rollback

Revert only the password rule, validation-message, and focused-test changes. No migration or deployment rollback is designed.
